tasks.title: Carry the target binding through local operation seams
tasks.goal: Carry an opt-in target binding through strict local operation records and refuse bound effects until the physical owner grants pinned roots.
steps: Trace existing deploy/native and extension request carriers, add an optional typed binding without changing legacy local operation meaning or serialized None bytes.

Use host-issued context/target binding values from M-16 conventions; keep a distinct bound state key, include binding in bound plan hash, and validate intent, receipt, native request and structured inspection equality before replay.

Refuse bound apply before inverse recovery, provider selection or state creation when no pinned host root/effect grant exists; never derive one from a request body or package descriptor. C.2 supplies the first supported bound effect.
positive_cases: The same package under two injected instance bindings gets distinct state keys and typed receipt/inspection identities without touching either destination.
A legacy local compatibility request keeps the incumbent projected files and byte-compatible unbound records.
negative_cases: A request body path or package descriptor self-grants a new root.
A copied legacy or other-instance receipt is accepted under a bound key, or unsupported bound apply reaches recovery/provider.

tasks.title: Fence aliased roots and stale target generations
tasks.goal: Fence aliased physical roots and stale target generations with pinned, lock-scoped capabilities; preserve safe refusal before the first bound effect.
steps: Extend the existing physical resource identity/lease boundary to recognize equivalent roots across environment instances.
Revalidate root handle, principal, generation and resource ownership at admission and commit; keep logical config-member ownership under a shared physical file lock.
Add temporary-root concurrency/replay tests covering alias roots, relocated directories and third-state changes; record exact partial truth if drift occurs after a landed write.
Prepare the pinned builtin provider and optional bound sidecar/checkpoint/inverse carriers; refuse actual bound publication until C.3 threads a host grant through the incumbent transaction.
positive_cases: Disjoint injected homes can proceed independently.
Two aliases of one root conflict even when their logical instance IDs differ.
negative_cases: Expired generation or changed root reuses an earlier plan.
Equal file bytes transfer ownership between receipt families.
An unsupported or mismatched bound operation reaches a provider effect before C.3.

tasks.title: Apply the first host-admitted bound builtin through the incumbent engine
tasks.goal: Thread a host-issued effect grant and pinned roots through the incumbent deploy transaction for the first successful local UserProfile vibe-bin operation.
steps: Require trusted host admission before inverse recovery, provider selection and state creation; bind the request, plan, physical resources and generation to one live destination lock.

Use the pinned project artifact, settings, bin and store handles in the incumbent provider apply/verify path; publish payload, launcher and pointer with existing checkpoints and retain the lock through receipt/commit.
Carry the exact operation binding through intent, pending/committed lock sidecar, checkpoints, inverse, receipt and inspection; legacy None bytes remain unchanged.

Limit first support to local UserProfile builtin deploy:vibe-bin with project-root artifact evidence and no prior bound generation. Refuse native/plugin/skill, slot/store-relative artifacts and unsupported recovery/remove until equivalent admission exists.
Report a landed write without final receipt as partial/uncertain with retained intent; never reconstruct bound sidecars from legacy fallback.
positive_cases: The same package bytes deployed into two disjoint injected homes create distinct physical outputs and bound receipts under their admitted principals.
Two aliases of one physical root cannot simultaneously publish through distinct logical bindings.
A legacy unbound operation retains its existing byte-compatible records and behavior.
negative_cases: Changed request body root, principal, target generation or provider scope reaches a bound effect after grant issuance.
A copied bound sidecar, checkpoint, inverse or receipt from another instance is replayed.
An interrupted bound write is reported as no-effects or reconstructed through a legacy fallback.
Unsupported native/plugin/skill or unadmitted artifact source reaches a bound provider effect.
